Comparing Roofing Warranties: What You Need to Know Before Signing

16 November 2024 Roofing

When it comes to roofing your home in Allentown, PA, making sense of roofing warranties can feel like solving a puzzle. However, understanding the details of a roofing warranty is critical for protecting your home and your investment. The right warranty can save you from costly repairs and give you peace of mind, especially with unpredictable weather.

This guide explains everything you need to know about roofing warranties, what they are, why they matter, and what to watch for before signing any agreements. Whether you need Roof Repair, Roof Replacement, Roof Installation, or Storm Damage Roof Repair, knowing the warranty options available can help you make a smarter decision.

What is a Roofing Warranty and Why Does It Matter?

A roofing warranty is a promise from a manufacturer or contractor to cover certain issues that might occur after your roof is installed. Think of it as a safety net that protects you from unexpected expenses. Warranties can cover problems related to materials, installation errors, or the entire roofing system. Without one, you could end up paying out of pocket for costly repairs.

For homeowners in Allentown, PA, a roofing warranty can be a deal-breaker. Harsh winters, heavy rainfall, and summer storms can cause significant roof damage. That’s why having a warranty in place can protect your home and keep your budget intact.

Types of Roofing Warranties You Should Know

Manufacturer’s Material Warranty

This type of warranty covers defects in the roofing materials. For example, if the shingles crack, warp, or fail due to a production error, the manufacturer will provide replacements. It’s worth noting that this warranty does not cover damage caused by improper installation.

Workmanship Warranty

If your roof is installed incorrectly, a workmanship warranty will have you covered. This warranty is issued by the roofing contractor rather than the material manufacturer. Companies in Allentown like In The Light Roofing often offer workmanship warranties as a mark of quality and trust in their services.

Full System Warranty

A full system warranty provides complete coverage for materials, labor, and workmanship. It’s like a “one-stop” warranty that handles all aspects of your roof. If you want complete peace of mind, this is a strong option to consider. Full system warranties are often provided by well-established roofing contractors or premium roofing system manufacturers.

What Questions Should You Ask Before Signing a Roofing Warranty?

Before you sign a roofing warranty, make sure you have answers to these important questions:

  • What does the warranty cover (materials, labor, or both)?
  • How long does the warranty last?
  • Are there any specific conditions or exclusions I should know about?
  • Is the warranty transferable if I sell my home?
  • Will I need to schedule regular maintenance to keep the warranty active?

These questions will help you avoid confusion and ensure you fully understand what you’re agreeing to before signing.

Factors That Can Void a Roofing Warranty

It’s easy to assume that once you have a roofing warranty, you’re protected from anything that goes wrong. However, warranties have rules and conditions. Failing to follow them could result in your coverage being voided. Here’s what to avoid:

  • DIY Roof Repairs: Attempting to repair your roof yourself can immediately void a warranty. Always hire a professional for Roof Repair or Storm Damage Roof Repair.
  • Lack of Maintenance: Some warranties require regular inspections or maintenance to remain valid. Skipping these inspections could lead to warranty cancellation.
  • Improper Ventilation: Poor attic ventilation can cause roofing materials to fail prematurely. This is often listed as an exclusion in roofing warranties.
  • Unauthorized Alterations: Adding solar panels, satellite dishes, or skylights without approval from your roofing contractor could void the warranty.

To protect your coverage, work with certified roofing professionals like In The Light Roofing and schedule regular roof inspections.

How Long Do Roofing Warranties Last?

The length of a roofing warranty depends on the type of warranty and the materials used. Here’s a breakdown:

  • Material Warranties: Typically last between 20 and 50 years, depending on the quality of the shingles.
  • Workmanship Warranties: Generally range from 5 to 25 years, depending on the contractor and the quality of installation.
  • Full System Warranties: These can last anywhere from 10 to 30 years, providing extensive coverage for both materials and labor.

If you plan to sell your home, it’s smart to choose a warranty that is transferable. This allows the new owner to benefit from the warranty, potentially increasing your home’s resale value.

Roofing Warranty vs. Homeowners Insurance: What’s the Difference?

Many homeowners confuse roofing warranties with homeowners insurance. While both offer protection, they serve different purposes:

  • Roofing Warranties cover manufacturing defects, installation errors, and system failures.
  • Homeowners Insurance covers weather-related damage caused by events like storms, hail, and falling trees.

If your roof is damaged in a storm, a warranty likely won’t cover it, but your homeowner’s insurance might. That’s why it’s important to have both in place.

What Can Homeowners Do to Protect Their Warranty?

Protecting your roofing warranty requires regular maintenance and smart decisions. Here’s how you can keep your warranty intact:

  • Schedule Annual Inspections: Hiring a local contractor like In The Light Roofing to inspect your roof each year ensures that small problems are fixed before they become big issues.
  • Keep Maintenance Records: If warranty claims require proof of regular inspections, you’ll need to provide records of previous maintenance.
  • Avoid Unauthorized Repairs: Only hire licensed roofing professionals for Roof Replacement, Roof Installation, and Storm Damage Roof Repair to avoid warranty violations.

Why Local Experience Matters for Roofing Warranties?

Hiring a local roofing contractor from Allentown, PA, gives you access to experienced professionals who understand the area’s weather, building codes, and common roofing issues. Local companies like In The Light Roofing know how to work with conditions unique to Allentown and offer warranties tailored to those conditions. Plus, they’re always nearby if you need service, inspections, or warranty claims.

Conclusion

Roofing warranties are essential for protecting your investment and avoiding surprise expenses. By understanding the different types of warranties and how they work, you can choose the best option for your home in Allentown, PA. Before you sign a warranty, ask questions, read the terms carefully, and ensure you’re working with a reputable contractor like In The Light Roofing.

If you ever need Roof Repair, Roof Replacement, Roof Installation, or Storm Damage Roof Repair, choose a contractor that offers clear warranty coverage to protect your home for years to come.

Frequently Asked Questions

How do I know if my roof warranty is still valid?

Check the warranty documentation or contact your roofing contractor. They can review the terms and let you know if you’re still covered.

Can I transfer my roofing warranty to a new homeowner?

Yes, some warranties are transferable, but not all of them. If you’re planning to sell your home, look for a warranty that can be passed to the new buyer.

Does a roofing warranty cover damage caused by a storm?

No, storm damage is typically covered by homeowners insurance, not a roofing warranty. For storm-related issues, you’ll need a service like Storm Damage Roof Repair.

What should I do if my roof is leaking?

Call a roofing professional for Roof Repair immediately. Don’t attempt to fix it yourself, as it could void your warranty. A licensed contractor can assess the damage and provide a repair plan.

Do I need to maintain my roof for the warranty to stay active?

Yes, many warranties require annual inspections or maintenance. It’s a good idea to hire a professional to inspect the roof at least once a year.

What’s the difference between a contractor warranty and a manufacturer warranty?

A manufacturer warranty covers defects in the roofing materials, while a contractor warranty covers workmanship. Ideally, you should have both.
